interactions.title: Recalled doppelganger plot and the weakening prison
lines: DM: You recall now, as you wait tensely for news from Kenzo—the Kenzo clone—the information you've recently learned about Apollyon's doppelgangers, the clones of you and your party that were apparently created by some twisted magic of Apollyon.

DM: You had heard news of them quite some time ago, about 2 weeks ago, when the Delwath doppelganger and Kenzo doppelganger attacked Chardon and opened a rift to Pandemonium, using Fausto's Pandemonium Skull. But since then you've learned considerably more.

DM: When you return to Vindristjarna from the Elemental Plane of Water, you learn from your crew that a Seeker clone had attacked the skyship, killing Yota and Igol, who are resurrected by Riswynn, before being defeated largely by Faldrak and the ice turrets.

DM: You also learn from Sura that a—another clone of Wellby rampaging across the Nevos Sea as a pirate, killing indiscriminately, and a clone of Riswynn, you learned from the dwarves of Tharn Todor, was a—was a—had come into Tharn Todor, the main dwarven city, apparently recruiting dwarves for some mission to the depths, which you inferred was a suicide mission.

DM: And the common thread between all of these that you, Delwath, I think, pieced together from talking to the Yota and Igol after they were resurrected, and from watching the dust of Seeker's doppelganger in the mirror, was that the souls of the people killed by the doppelgangers are transported somehow to the magical box that holds Apollyon in his tomb. And as they struggle for freedom, they chip away at the bonds that hold it in place.
DM: So each time a doppelganger kills, the bonds holding Apollyon in place grow weaker and weaker.
Seeker: So we have to stop them.

DM: The souls don't all meet. Everybody who dies doesn't immediately leave the lock. Like, if you recall, Yota like stuck around for a while and didn't try and break free. And so there's a—the number of souls that are probably trapped in the locks at the moment.

DM: You also learned that the doppelgangers seem to have some kind of item or ward that keeps them from dying, and safely returns them to Apollyon because when you scried on the Delwath and Kenzo Clones, you saw them pacing the docks at what you presumed was the city of Drankor.

interactions.title: The jade’s journey into a storm in Kenzo’s dream
lines: DM: So you settle in for the night. That evening, in addition to the normal dreams of Apollyon slowly breaking through from his prison—

DM: Kenzo, you have a dream of the jade. Jade you're flying to is cracking and bubbling, turning into a mist that floats out of this red sandstone cave, drifting above the jungle. Everything's dark and still until a strong wind sweeps up, and the jade mist swirls and blows across the canopy. You're swept with it and you watch the canopy pass below you, and you see the twinkling of the ocean waves crashing below you, despite the clear skies and seeming lack of winds.

DM: In the light of the waxing crescent moon. And then you're quickly blown offshore, swooping past mangroves and over the shoals, your sense of time and distance distorted in the greenscape—dreamscape—until—
